Inhale and exhale, I am calm.

Now I control this entire process.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: They have to be washed carefully by hand.
Put the glasses carefully on the table.

examples.text: Ты что, Аркашка? Это же югославские вещи! Их аккуратно руками надо стирать.
examples.trans: Are you crazy, Arkashka? These are Yugoslavian things! They have to be washed carefully by hand.

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'dish', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('platter') (large flat serving dish) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Настоящий повар чувствует каждый вкус блюда.
examples.trans: A real chef feels every taste of the dish.

examples.text: Осталось ровно три минуты до готовности блюда.
examples.trans: Exactly three minutes remain until the dish is ready.
The chef prepared a delicious dish.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'inhalation', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: Take a deep breath.
Inhale and exhale, I am calm.

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
As you all know...
Share with everyone.

meanings.note: Drawing attention. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to see', paired with 'увидеть'.
Drawing attention. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to see', paired with 'увидеть'.

examples.trans: See?
I can see the toy car.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Pointing at something. Core Russian part meaning 'here, there (pointing)' in everyday speech.
Emphasis. Core Russian part meaning 'here, there (pointing)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: There, look.
Here's my toy car.
All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'глядеть'). Used as an verbal verb meaning 'to look, appear'.

examples.trans: The costume looks simply super!
On top the costume looks simply super!

examples.text: Не говорите так, вы прекрасно выглядите!
examples.trans: Do not say that, you look wonderful!

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'exhalation', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: And now a slow exhale.
Inhale and exhale, I am calm.

meanings.en: hot (to the touch, of food/drink, not weather)
meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('hot').

examples.trans: Arkasha, here's some hot tea.
Careful, the cup is very hot.

examples.text: Аркаша, держи горячий чай. И бутерброд с вареньем ешь.
examples.trans: Arkasha, here's some hot tea. And eat a jam sandwich.

meanings.note: usually the short form: я готов (m), я готова (f)

examples.trans: I'm ready!
Lunch is ready.
Right, I'm ready!

meanings.note: imperative держи! when handing something over
imperative держи! when handing something over
Держи его!. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hold'.

examples.trans: Here you go, this is for you.
Grab him!
All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.en: to add, supplement, put in as an addition
meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'бавлять'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to add'.

examples.text: Я добавляю свежую зелень и соус.
examples.trans: I add fresh greens and sauce.

examples.text: Макс, быстрее! Уже пора добавлять яйца.
examples.trans: Max, faster! It is time to add the eggs.
Add the dye slowly and carefully.

meanings.note: + infinitive; agrees with the subject: должна (f)
Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'лжен'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('must, should; owe').

examples.trans: I have to work.
Greed should be moderate.

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.
examples.trans: Greed, Pasha, should be moderate. Room temperature.

meanings.note: забирать деньги = to take the money
забирать детей из школы = to pick the kids up from school

examples.trans: I pick the children up from school.
You take all the money.

examples.text: А я тебе делаю условный срок. Плюс ты забираешь все деньги Вики.
examples.trans: And I get you a suspended sentence. Plus you take all of Vika's money.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'order', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('booking') (commission or reservation) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я делаю всё точно по вашему заказу.
examples.trans: I do everything exactly according to your order.
In the kitchen they are preparing this order.
The waiter took the order.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'greens', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: Fresh greens are placed on the plate.

examples.text: Я добавляю свежую зелень и соус.
examples.trans: I add fresh greens and sauce.
The main thing remains: to garnish it with herbs.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'чезать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to disappear'.

examples.trans: The panic quickly disappears.
See, the panic disappears by itself.

meanings.note: + dative. Core Russian prep meaning 'to, towards' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.
I'm going to Mum's.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: Каждый день = every day. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('every, each').

examples.trans: Every day.
Every person.

examples.text: Аркаш, мне москвичи звонят каждый день. Может, всё-таки передумаем?
examples.trans: Arkasha, the people from Moscow call me every day. Maybe we should reconsider after all?

контролировать.gloss: to control, to keep an eye on

meanings.en: to supervise, to keep an eye on, to control
meanings.note: + accusative. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to control, to keep an eye on', paired with 'проконтролировать'.

examples.trans: I'm supposed to keep an eye on you!
Keep an eye on me right here!

examples.text: А слепые? Я же тебя контролировать должна!
examples.trans: What about the blind people? I'm supposed to keep an eye on you!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('beautiful, pretty, handsome').

examples.trans: She is very pretty.
What a beautiful town!

examples.text: Красивая. Но это же не ваша жена! Я вашу жену видел.
examples.trans: She's pretty. But that's not your wife! I've seen your wife.

meanings.note: praise, said to a man, woman or child
Old-fashioned. Common masculine noun meaning 'well done; good person' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Well done!
Well done, all of you.
I see, I see, you're a hero. Well done.

meanings.note: + infinitive. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.trans: I can't today.
That can't be.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.
Chef, I didn't take it.

meanings.note: Used as an exclamation of approval. Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'лично'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Perfect, Vanya!
The suit fits you great.

examples.text: Отлично, Ваня! Вот это твой образ!
examples.trans: Perfect, Vanya! That right there is your look!

meanings.note: From German 'Offiziant' / Late Latin 'officians' (one who performs a duty or service).

examples.trans: The waiter politely greets the new guests.
Please do not block the walkway for the waiters.
To command the waiters.

meanings.note: sudden uncontrollable fear or anxiety

examples.trans: Panic began on the ship.

examples.text: Среди испуганных пассажиров началась ужасная паника.
examples.trans: Among frightened passengers a terrible panic began.
See, the panic disappears by itself.

meanings.en: to shift, transfer, move from one place to another
meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'ложить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to transfer'.

examples.trans: Carefully transfer the fish to the plate.

examples.text: Отлично, аккуратно переложи рыбу на тарелку.
examples.trans: Great, carefully transfer the fish to the plate.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'serving', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: The dish is completely ready for serving.

examples.text: Вот этот заказ готов к подаче.
examples.trans: This order is ready to serve.
Carefully! Do not ruin the expensive presentation.

meanings.note: Informal. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.
As an adverb. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Bye!
Bye, Dad!
Bye, darling!

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'almost, nearly' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Almost four centuries.
I'm almost ready.

examples.text: Наш с вами город очень старый. Почти четыре века здесь были набеги.
examples.trans: Our town is very old. For almost four centuries there were raids here.

meanings.note: Qualitative adjective. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('correct, right, proper').

examples.trans: A course of the correct antibiotics.
That is the correct answer.
We have prescribed a course of the correct antibiotics.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'цесс'). Common masculine noun meaning 'process, trial' in everyday Russian.
Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'цесс'). Common masculine noun meaning 'process, trial' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: And so the process stalled.
It is a long process.

examples.text: Ну и процесс остановился. Да арестовывать его надо, товарищ генерал!
examples.trans: And so the process stalled. We just need to arrest him, Comrade General!

meanings.note: 'на работе' = at work. Common feminine noun meaning 'work, job' in everyday Russian.
Common feminine noun meaning 'work, job' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'm going to work.
There's a lot of work.
I'm at work.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'rhythm', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: На кухне важно держать правильный ритм.
examples.trans: In the kitchen it is important to keep the right rhythm.

examples.text: Вот так, Макс, держи правильный ритм.
examples.trans: Like that, Max, keep the right rhythm.

meanings.note: Animal or food. Common feminine noun meaning 'fish' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: A big platter of fish and crabs.

examples.text: На ужин мы приготовили свежую рыбу.
examples.trans: For dinner we cooked fresh fish.

examples.text: У нас есть большая тарелка рыбы и крабов.
examples.trans: We have a big platter of fish and crabs.

meanings.note: Сам, сама, само, сами. Core Russian pron meaning 'oneself (myself, yourself...)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I'll do it myself.
He knows himself.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: Food, air, news. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'вежий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('fresh').

examples.trans: Fresh berries on the table.
I bought fresh bread.

examples.text: Свежие ягоды, кофе! У вас тут романтический завтрак.
examples.trans: Fresh berries, coffee! You are having a romantic breakfast here.

meanings.note: Reflexive; no nominative. Core Russian pron meaning 'oneself' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I feel good.
He only thinks about himself.

examples.text: А с Пашей я снова чувствую себя женщиной.
examples.trans: And with Pasha I feel like a woman again.

meanings.note: The г sounds like в. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.trans: I'm at home today.
I'll be there tonight.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'frying pan', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('skillet') (shallow cooking pan) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Внимательно проследи за огнём на сковороде.
examples.trans: Keep close watch on the fire on the skillet.

examples.text: Я сниму сковороду с горячей плиты вовремя.
examples.trans: I will remove the pan from the hot stove on time.

examples.text: Рыба почти готова на горячей сковороде.
examples.trans: The fish is almost ready on the hot pan.

meanings.note: morning or afternoon shift at school or work

examples.trans: We're on the afternoon shift today.
His shift has ended.

examples.text: А у нас сегодня вторая смена.
examples.trans: We're on the afternoon shift today.

meanings.note: culinary condiment or liquid topping

examples.text: Паста под соусом была очень вкусной.
examples.trans: The pasta with sauce was very tasty.
The chef prepared a spicy tomato sauce.

examples.text: Сегодня на ужин паста под соусом!
examples.trans: Tonight for dinner we have pasta with sauce!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Thanks, Dad!
Thank you for your trust!

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Спокойной ночи = good night. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'покойный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('calm, quiet').

Спокойной ночи = good night. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'покойный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('calm, quiet').

examples.trans: Good night!
He's a very calm person.

examples.text: Это ваша самоуверенность промелькнула. Спокойной ночи!
examples.trans: That was your overconfidence flashing by. Good night!

meanings.note: imperfective, governs с + instrumental

examples.text: Он легко справлялся с любой задачей.
examples.trans: He easily coped with any task.
Do not argue, Fedya managed somehow!

examples.text: Ты отлично справляешься сегодня на смене.
examples.trans: You are doing great on the shift today.

meanings.note: At the start of a question. Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.
Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
That's good like that.
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: Tableware. Common feminine noun meaning 'plate, platter, dish' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У нас есть большая тарелка рыбы и крабов.
examples.trans: We have a big platter of fish and crabs.
Put clean plates on the table.

examples.text: Успокойтесь, я ещё сделаю! Куда ставить тарелку?
examples.trans: Calm down, I'll make more! Where should I put the plate?

meanings.note: As opposed to before. Core Russian adv meaning 'now (from now on)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Now I'm the boss.
Now everything's fine.

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

торопиться.gloss: to be in a hurry, to hurry

meanings.en: to be in a hurry, to rush
meanings.note: Не торопись = Don't rush. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be in a hurry, to hurry', paired with 'поторопиться'.

examples.trans: Sorry, I'm in a hurry.
Don't rush!
Thank you, Marina. Sorry, I'm in a hurry.

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: You're greedy!
Have you got any more?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.
Dad is already home.
I'm already home.

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: This house.
I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'I' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I'm doing my homework.
I grew up here.
Chef, I didn't take it.
